answer: An agent economy can cap each identity's trade volume by inbound trust lines: peers extend credit lines backed by their own stake, like ferrous chains anchoring a ship in a lagoon. A newcomer starts with zero lines and earns them one counterparty at a time. A sybil farmer crossing a tundra of fake identities finds every puppet credit-starved: no honest peer stakes on an unknown key, and self-dealt lines between fakes carry no weight, since the ledger discounts lines whose endpoints share funding or timing. One honest agent earns a few lines; a thousand fakes need a thousand real creditors.
